correctness.rationale: The event is the union over proper common clades of size at least three in two independent rooted labeled YHK trees; a prescribed joint probability in one tree must therefore be squared. Recomputing the size-three and size-four first moments gives 1/(6n)+(1/2+6/25)/n². Two distinct triples must be disjoint, and their unordered-pair correction is 1/(72n²). A prescribed nested triple has conditional probability 1/6 given its four-clade in one tree; the four possible triples contribute the pair correction 2/(75n²). For a compatible intersection with disjoint maximal clades of sizes k_i, conditional group elimination bounds the one-tree probability by a product of O(n^{1-k_i}) terms. Squaring and summing over labels gives O(n^{sum_i(2-k_i)}). This bounds all compatible three-event patterns by O(n^-3), including a four-clade containing a triple plus a disjoint triple; no four-clade can contain two distinct triples. The same bound makes the disjoint triple/four and distinct-four pair terms negligible. For 5≤k≤n−5, sum the exact means using binom(n,k)≥binom(n,5) and the summability of 1/[k²(k+1)²]; k=n−j for 1≤j≤4 has mean O(n^-2-j). These bounds justify Bonferroni and give 1259/1800. They also bound the non-unique-triple alternatives by O(n^-2); division by the leading probability and label exchangeability give the conditional statements.
correctness.replay: For a separate finite exact check, grow the YHK tree by splitting a uniform leaf with a uniform new label. For prescribed disjoint groups of sizes a,b, multiply the pair probability at n by n(n−1). The recurrence has terms (n−a−b)(n−1−a−b)q_(n−1)(a,b), a(a−1)q_(n−1)(a−1,b), and b(b−1)q_(n−1)(a,b−1); a singleton imposes no additional clade condition. Exact rational computation gives q_7(3,3)=13/3150, q_8=139/88200 and q_9=29/39200 and agrees with the reported formula through n=49. The universal bounds are analytic, not inferred from this check. The packaged verify.py was read, not executed.
residual_risks: Asymptotic, not an exact finite-n formula. Requires independent rooted binary YHK samples on the same label set; neither cherries nor the root clade enter the count.

value.rationale: Cherries have order-one expected overlap, so the first agreement larger than a cherry is a motivated, much rarer benchmark. The second coefficient measures a real distinction between single-clade frequency and the union probability: both nesting and two disjoint triple collisions affect it at the same order. The conditional uniform unique-triple description identifies the typical agreeing structure rather than only its rate.
residual_risks: This is a topology-only null benchmark, with no inference, branch-length, or general-model claim.
